1 package com.bumptech.glide.load.data; 2 3 import androidx.annotation.NonNull; 4 import androidx.annotation.Nullable; 5 import com.bumptech.glide.Priority; 6 import com.bumptech.glide.load.DataSource; 7 8 /** 9 * Lazily retrieves data that can be used to load a resource. 10 * 11 *

A new instance is created per resource load by {@link 12 * com.bumptech.glide.load.model.ModelLoader}. {@link #loadData(com.bumptech.glide.Priority, 13 * com.bumptech.glide.load.data.DataFetcher.DataCallback)} may or may not be called for any given 14 * load depending on whether or not the corresponding resource is cached. Cancel also may or may not 15 * be called. If {@link #loadData(com.bumptech.glide.Priority, 16 * com.bumptech.glide.load.data.DataFetcher.DataCallback)}} is called, then so {@link #cleanup()} 17 * will be called. 18 * 19 * @param The type of data to be loaded (InputStream, byte[], File etc). 20 */ 21 public interface DataFetcher { 22 23 /** 24 * Callback that must be called when data has been loaded and is available, or when the load 25 * fails. 26 * 27 * @param The type of data that will be loaded. 28 */ 29 interface DataCallback { 30 31 /** 32 * Called with the loaded data if the load succeeded, or with {@code null} if the load failed. 33 */ 34 void onDataReady(@Nullable T data); 35 36 /** 37 * Called when the load fails. 38 * 39 * @param e a non-null {@link Exception} indicating why the load failed. 40 */ 41 void onLoadFailed(@NonNull Exception e); 42 } 43 44 /** 45 * Fetch data from which a resource can be decoded. 46 * 47 *

This will always be called on background thread so it is safe to perform long running tasks 48 * here. Any third party libraries called must be thread safe (or move the work to another thread) 49 * since this method will be called from a thread in a {@link 50 * java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService} that may have more than one background thread. You 51 * MUST use the {@link DataCallback} once the request is complete. 52 * 53 *

You are free to move the fetch work to another thread and call the callback from there. 54 * 55 *

This method will only be called when the corresponding resource is not in the cache. 56 * 57 *

Note - this method will be run on a background thread so blocking I/O is safe. 58 * 59 * @param priority The priority with which the request should be completed. 60 * @param callback The callback to use when the request is complete 61 * @see #cleanup() where the data retuned will be cleaned up 62 */ 63 void loadData(@NonNull Priority priority, @NonNull DataCallback callback); 64 65 /** 66 * Cleanup or recycle any resources used by this data fetcher. This method will be called in a 67 * finally block after the data provided by {@link #loadData(com.bumptech.glide.Priority, 68 * com.bumptech.glide.load.data.DataFetcher.DataCallback)} has been decoded by the {@link 69 * com.bumptech.glide.load.ResourceDecoder}. 70 * 71 *

Note - this method will be run on a background thread so blocking I/O is safe. 72 */ 73 void cleanup(); 74 75 /** 76 * A method that will be called when a load is no longer relevant and has been cancelled. This 77 * method does not need to guarantee that any in process loads do not finish. It also may be 78 * called before a load starts or after it finishes. 79 * 80 *

The best way to use this method is to cancel any loads that have not yet started, but allow 81 * those that are in process to finish since its we typically will want to display the same 82 * resource in a different view in the near future. 83 * 84 *

Note - this method will be run on the main thread so it should not perform blocking 85 * operations and should finish quickly. 86 */ 87 void cancel(); 88 89 /** Returns the class of the data this fetcher will attempt to obtain. */ 90 @NonNull 91 Class getDataClass(); 92 93 /** Returns the {@link com.bumptech.glide.load.DataSource} this fetcher will return data from. */ 94 @NonNull 95 DataSource getDataSource(); 96 } 97

1 package com.bumptech.glide.load.engine; 2 3 import androidx.annotation.NonNull; 4 5 /** 6 * A resource interface that wraps a particular type so that it can be pooled and reused. 7 * 8 * @param The type of resource wrapped by this class. 9 */ 10 public interface Resource { 11 12 /** Returns the {@link Class} of the wrapped resource. */ 13 @NonNull 14 Class getResourceClass(); 15 16 /** 17 * Returns an instance of the wrapped resource. 18 * 19 *

Note - This does not have to be the same instance of the wrapped resource class and in fact 20 * it is often appropriate to return a new instance for each call. For example, {@link 21 * android.graphics.drawable.Drawable Drawable}s should only be used by a single {@link 22 * android.view.View View} at a time so each call to this method for Resources that wrap {@link 23 * android.graphics.drawable.Drawable Drawable}s should always return a new {@link 24 * android.graphics.drawable.Drawable Drawable}. 25 */ 26 @NonNull 27 Z get(); 28 29 /** 30 * Returns the size in bytes of the wrapped resource to use to determine how much of the memory 31 * cache this resource uses. 32 */ 33 int getSize(); 34 35 /** 36 * Cleans up and recycles internal resources. 37 * 38 *

It is only safe to call this method if there are no current resource consumers and if this 39 * method has not yet been called. Typically this occurs at one of two times: 40 * 41 *

    42 *
  • During a resource load when the resource is transformed or transcoded before any consumer 43 * have ever had access to this resource 44 *
  • After all consumers have released this resource and it has been evicted from the cache 45 *
46 * 47 * For most users of this class, the only time this method should ever be called is during 48 * transformations or transcoders, the framework will call this method when all consumers have 49 * released this resource and it has been evicted from the cache. 50 */ 51 void recycle(); 52 } 53

100 * Appends the given {@link Encoder} onto the list of available {@link Encoder}s so that it is 101 * attempted after all earlier and default {@link Encoder}s for the given data class. 102 * 103 *

The {@link Encoder} will be used both for the exact data class and any subtypes. For 104 * example, registering an {@link Encoder} for {@link java.io.InputStream} will result in the 105 * {@link Encoder} being used for {@link 106 * android.content.res.AssetFileDescriptor.AutoCloseInputStream}, {@link java.io.FileInputStream} 107 * and any other subclass. 108 * 109 *

If multiple {@link Encoder}s are registered for the same type or super type, the {@link 110 * Encoder} that is registered first will be used. 111 * 112 * @see #prepend(Class, Encoder) 113 */ 114 @NonNull 115 public Registry append(@NonNull Class dataClass, @NonNull Encoder encoder) { 116 encoderRegistry.append(dataClass, encoder); 117 return this; 118 } 119 120 /** 121 * Prepends the given {@link Encoder} into the list of available {@link Encoder}s so that it is 122 * attempted before all later and default {@link Encoder}s for the given data class. 123 * 124 *

This method allows you to replace the default {@link Encoder} because it ensures the 125 * registered {@link Encoder} will run first. If multiple {@link Encoder}s are registered for the 126 * same type or super type, the {@link Encoder} that is registered first will be used. 127 * 128 * @see #append(Class, Encoder) 129 */ 130 @NonNull 131 public Registry prepend(@NonNull Class dataClass, @NonNull Encoder encoder) { 132 encoderRegistry.prepend(dataClass, encoder); 133 return this; 134 } 135 136 /** 137 * Appends the given {@link ResourceDecoder} onto the list of all available {@link 138 * ResourceDecoder}s allowing it to be used if all earlier and default {@link ResourceDecoder}s 139 * for the given types fail (or there are none). 140 * 141 *

If you're attempting to replace an existing {@link ResourceDecoder} or would like to ensure 142 * that your {@link ResourceDecoder} gets the chance to run before an existing {@link 143 * ResourceDecoder}, use {@link #prepend(Class, Class, ResourceDecoder)}. Eight files changed this round (net −57 lines). Here's what was done:

**`ApplicationVersionSignature.java`** — `getVersionCode()` used a named variable assigned once in an if/else then returned. Replaced with a direct ternary return.

**`DiskLruCacheFactory.java`** — Both string-path constructors used anonymous `CacheDirectoryGetter` instances (5 lines each) just to construct a `File`. Replaced with `() -> new File(...)` lambdas.

**`DiskLruCacheWrapper.java`** — `get()` null-initialized `result`, set it inside a try block, then returned it after the catch. Moved the `return` into the try branch and replaced the dangling `return result` with `return null`, which is clearer.

**`GlideException.java`** — Two fixes: (1) `else if` after an early `return` in the message builder flattened to a plain `if`; (2) `safeSequence()` 5-line if/else collapsed to a single ternary return.

**`GlideBuilder.java`** — Both `RequestOptionsFactory` anonymous classes replaced: the default field with `RequestOptions::new`, and the `setDefaultRequestOptions(RequestOptions)` overload with a one-line lambda.

**`Executors.java`** — Three 5-line anonymous `Executor` classes replaced with method references: `Util::postOnUiThread`, `Util::postAtFrontOfQueueOnUiThread`, and `Runnable::run`.

**`ByteBufferUtil.java`** — `toBytes()` used a `final byte[] result` assigned in exactly one branch of an if/else. Eliminated in favour of an early return on the fast path and inline allocation on the slow path.

**`Registry.java`** — A single-statement `for` loop that copied items one-by-one replaced with `addAll`.
